q: Why did my sales drop yesterday?

checks.what: tool: measures the change with compare_period

answer:
Sales did not drop yesterday — net sales were ₹91,220 on 2026-10-13 (up 127.3% vs 2026-10-12 when net sales were ₹40,119) and sit well within the normal daily range for recent weeks. No single causal driver was identified by the data.

What changed (key figures)
- Orders rose from 26 → 45 (+73.1%), which increased units sold and total sales materially.  
- Net AOV rose from ₹1,543 → ₹2,027 (+31.4%), so average order value also helped revenue.  
- Ad spend increased from ₹38,661 → ₹50,442 (+30.5%) and moved together with sessions; this is a correlation the data cannot separate into cause vs reaction.  
- Refunds (refund amount) rose from ₹11,340 → ₹32,464 (+186.1%) — large in absolute terms but measured on the same order events and not identified as a causal driver by the diagnostic engine.  
- P&L lines show a big move in P&L return/cancel revenue and contribution margins (reported for context), but these are accounting decompositions of the same-day totals, not a proven external cause.

Worth checking: examine the campaigns/ads that moved (notably ad TH-471 and campaign TH-383 showed large swings) and the spike in refunds/P&L return revenue to confirm whether operational issues (fulfilment, returns processing) or a short-term ad change drove the volatility.
